chunks.arabic_text: سَهْلُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ شَمُّونٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ الْأَصَمِّ عَنْ مِسْمَعِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ

translations.en: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Mismā' ibn 'Abd al-Malik, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام.

chunks.arabic_text: أَنَّ أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ رُفِعَ إِلَيْهِ رَجُلٌ عَذَّبَ عَبْدَهُ حَتَّى مَاتَ فَضَرَبَهُ مِائَةً نَكَالًا وَحَبَسَهُ سَنَةً وَغَرَّمَهُ قِيمَةَ الْعَبْدِ فَتَصَدَّقَ بِهَا عَنْهُ

translations.en: That Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام was presented with the case of a man who had tortured his slave until he died. So he struck him with one hundred lashes as a deterrent, imprisoned him for a year, and fined him the value of the slave, then gave it in charity on his behalf.

en.summary: This hadith reports a judicial ruling of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام regarding a man who caused the death of his slave through torture. It demonstrates punishment for oppression, public deterrence, imprisonment, and financial liability, while also showing the protection of the rights of the enslaved under Islamic law.
en.seo_question: What was the ruling of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام on a master who tortured his slave to death?

key_terms.نَكَالًا: as a deterrent and exemplary punishment
key_terms.قِيمَةَ الْعَبْدِ: the monetary value of the slave as compensation
key_terms.فَتَصَدَّقَ بِهَا عَنْهُ: then he gave it as charity on his behalf
